baseline_answer_text:
Under the Constitution of Nepal, rights regarding education include the following:

**Right Relating to Education (Article 31):**
- Every citizen has the right of access to basic education [E2].
- Every citizen has the right to compulsory and free education up to the basic level, as well as free education up to the secondary level from the State [E1], [E2].
- Citizens with disabilities and indigent citizens have the right to obtain free higher education in accordance with law [E1], [E2].
- Visually impaired citizens have the right to receive free education through Braille script, and citizens with hearing or speaking impairments have the right to receive free education through sign language, in accordance with law [E1].
- Every Nepali community residing in Nepal has the right to receive education in its own mother tongue and, for that purpose, to establish and operate schools and educational institutes in accordance with law [E1].

**Education Rights Conferred to Specific Groups:**
- **Children:** Every child has the right to education, health, maintenance, proper care, sports, entertainment, and overall personality development from their families and the State [E3]. Additionally, no child may be subjected to physical, mental, or any other form of torture in a school, home, or any other place [E3].
- **Women:** Women have the right to obtain special opportunities in education, health, employment, and social security on the basis of positive discrimination [E3].
- **Dalit Community:** Provision must be made by law for free education with scholarships for Dalit students from primary to higher education, along with special legal provisions for the Dalit in technical and vocational education [E4].
- **Conflict Victims, Families of Martyrs, and Persons with Disabilities:** In accordance with law, prioritized opportunities—with justice and due respect—in education, health, employment, housing, and social security are guaranteed to the families of martyrs, disappeared persons, those disabled and injured in people's movements, armed conflicts, and revolutions, as well as democracy fighters, conflict victims, displaced persons, persons with disabilities, the injured, and victims [E5].

Under the Constitution of Nepal, rights regarding education include the following:

**Article 31: Right Relating to Education**
* **Access to Basic Education:** Every citizen has the right of access to basic education [E2].
* **Compulsory and Free Education:** Every citizen has the right to compulsory and free education up to the basic level, and free education up to the secondary level from the State [E1], [E2].
* **Higher Education for Specific Groups:** Citizens with disabilities and indigent citizens have the right to free higher education in accordance with law [E1], [E2].
* **Education for Persons with Sensory Impairments:** Visually impaired citizens have the right to free education through Braille script, and citizens with hearing or speaking impairment have the right to free education through sign language, in accordance with law [E1].
* **Mother Tongue Education:** Every Nepali community residing in Nepal has the right to get education in its own mother tongue and, for that purpose, to open and operate schools and educational institutes, in accordance with law [E1].

**Additional Education Rights Guaranteed under Other Articles**
* **Rights of Women:** Women have the right to obtain special opportunity in education (along with health, employment, and social security) on the basis of positive discrimination [E3].
* **Rights of the Child:** 
  * Every child has the right to education, health, maintenance, proper care, sports, entertainment, and overall personality development from families and the State [E3].
  * No child may be subjected to physical, mental, or any other form of torture in school, home, or any other place or condition [E3].
* **Rights of Dalit:** Provision of free education with scholarship from primary to higher education must be made by law for Dalit students, and special legal provisions must be made for the Dalit in technical and vocational education [E4].
* **Right to Social Justice (Prioritized Opportunity):** The families of martyrs, disappeared persons, those disabled and injured in people's movements, armed conflicts, and revolutions, democracy fighters, conflict victims and displaced persons, persons with disabilities, the injured, and victims have the right to get a prioritized opportunity, with justice and due respect, in education (as well as health, employment, housing, and social security) in accordance with law [E5].

baseline_answer_text:
According to the Act Relating to Compulsory and Free Education, 2075 (2018):

**Definitions and Scope**
* **Compulsory education** is defined as a mandatory provision for children of the age prescribed by the Government of Nepal to be admitted to schools or alternative educational institutions, and to regularly study and complete the basic level of study [E1]. Basic education covers school education from grade one to grade eight [E1].
* **Free education** is defined as education provided by a school or educational institution without receiving any fee under any heading from the student or guardian [E4].

**Provisions on Compulsory Education**
* **State and Local Level Obligation:** Following the commencement of the Act, the State must make provisions through every Local Level to provide compulsory education up to the basic level to every child who has completed four years of age but has not completed thirteen years of age [E2]. In addition, at least one year of early childhood development and education must be provided after completing the age of four years [E2].
* **Emergency/Disaster Safety:** The Local Level must make provisions to safely provide basic-level education to children affected by natural disasters, accidents, or unexpected incidents [E2].
* **State Liability:** The Government of Nepal, Provincial Government, and Local Level bear the liability to provide every citizen with basic-level education and make necessary arrangements, with the Government of Nepal leading and coordinating [E5]. The State also has the liability to provide every citizen with education up to the secondary level (grades nine to twelve or equivalent) [E4], [E5].
* **Duties of Citizens:** Every citizen has a duty to obtain basic-level education and a duty to regularly send their children of the relevant age group to school [E5].

**Provisions on Free Education**
* **Higher Education:** Citizens who are Dalit, have disabilities, and are economically destitute have the right to get free higher education [E5].
* **Reservations in Private and Public Trust Schools:** Every school with private investment and every school operated under a public educational trust must reserve seats to provide free education to students from early childhood development and education up to grade twelve based on total student enrollment [E3]:
  * At least 10% in schools with up to 500 students [E3];
  * At least 12% in schools with 500 to 800 students [E3];
  * At least 15% in schools with more than 800 students [E3].
* **Selection and Rights for Reserved Seats:** Children are admitted to these reserved seats based on competition among prescribed groups [E3]. Students studying free of charge in these seats are allowed to apply for free study or scholarships for grades or levels higher than the grade in which they acquired free education [E3]. Existing scholarships at the time of the Act’s commencement cannot be reduced [E3].

candidate_answer_text:
Under the Act Relating to Compulsory and Free Education, 2075 (2018), the law provides the following:

### Definitions
* **Compulsory Education:** A mandatory provision for children of the age prescribed by the Government of Nepal to be admitted to schools or alternative educational institutions to regularly study and complete basic level study [E1]. "Basic education" covers school education from grade one to grade eight [E1].
* **Free Education:** Education provided by a school or educational institution without receiving any fee under any heading from the student or guardian [E4].

### State Obligations and Compulsory Education Mandates
* **Compulsory Basic Education:** After the commencement of the Act, the State must make provisions through every Local Level to provide compulsory education up to the basic level to every child who has completed four years of age but has not completed thirteen years of age [E2]. 
* **Early Childhood Education:** In addition to basic education, at least one year of early childhood development and education must be provided after completing four years of age [E2].
* **Disaster and Incident Response:** Local Levels must make provisions to provide education up to the basic level safely for children affected by natural disasters, accidents, or unexpected incidents [E2].
* **State Liability:** The Government of Nepal, Provincial Government, and Local Level bear the liability to provide every citizen with education up to the basic level and to make necessary arrangements [E5]. The State also has the liability to provide education up to the secondary level (grade nine to grade twelve or equivalent), with the Government of Nepal providing necessary coordination and leadership [E4, E5].

### Duties of Citizens
* Every citizen has a duty to obtain basic level education [E5].
* Every citizen has a duty to send their children who are of the age group for acquiring basic education to school regularly [E5].

### Rights to Free and Special Education
* Citizens who are economically destitute, persons with disabilities, and Dalits have the right to get free higher education [E5].
* Children of martyrs, disappeared persons, conflict victims, the wounded, and persons with disabilities have the right to get special opportunities as prescribed [E5].
* Every child has the right to get quality education from qualified teachers [E5].

### Free Education Quotas in Private and Trust Schools
Every school with private investment and every school operated under a public educational trust must reserve seats to provide free education to students from early childhood development and education up to grade twelve, based on total student enrollment [E3]:
* **Up to 500 students:** At least 10 percent of seats [E3].
* **500 to 800 students:** At least 12 percent of seats [E3].
* **More than 800 students:** At least 15 percent of seats [E3].

Scholarships being provided by any school at the commencement of the Act must not be reduced [E3]. Qualified children are admitted to these reserved seats based on competition among prescribed groups, and students receiving this free education are permitted to apply for free study or scholarships for higher grades or levels pursuant to prevailing law [E3].

The Act Relating to Compulsory and Free Education, 2075 (2018)

Date of Publication in the Nepal Gazette 2075.6.2 (18 September 2018)

Act No. 16 of the year 2075 (2018) An Act Made to Provide for Compulsory and Free Education Preamble: Whereas, it is expedient to make legal provisions relating to compulsory and free education, in order to ensure easy and equal access and continuity of all to education, and to make education universal, useful for life, competitive and qualitative, while focusing education on the building of nation, being committed to socialism based on democratic values and norms, by implementing, on the ground, the basic human rights of every person to acquire education and the fundamental right conferred by the Constitution; Now, therefore, be it enacted by the Federal Parliament.

Chapter-1 Preliminary 1. Short title and commencement: (1) This Act may be cited as the “Act Relating to Compulsory and Free Education, 2075 (2018).”

(2) This Act shall commence at once. 2. Definitions: Unless the subject or context otherwise requires, in this Act, (a) "Compulsory education" means a mandatory provision to regularly study and complete basic level of study by the children of the age prescribed by the Government of Nepal, upon getting admitted to schools or other alternative educational institutions. (b) "Guardian" means the father, mother of a child or the person whose name is registered at the school as the guardian, and this term also includes his or her guardian or curator. (c) "Economically destitute" means the condition of having annual income that is less than the prescribed limit. (d) "Basic education" means the school education from grade one to grade eight.

Based on the supplied evidence from the *Economic Survey 2023/24*, the document reports the following regarding schools and students:

### 1. Student Enrollment, Retention, and Completion Indicators
* **Pre-Primary Education:** Total enrollment rates in pre-primary education range across reported periods from 77.7% to 99.9% [E2]. The percentage of new entrants in Grade 1 with pre-primary education experience ranges from 59.6% to 76.9% [E2].
* **Grade 1 Enrollment:** Total enrollment rates in Grade 1 range between 115.9% and 136.7%, while the net enrollment rate ranges between 93.9% and 97.3% [E2].
* **Grades 1–5 (Primary/Basic):** Total enrollment rates range from 118.2% to 135.4%, and net enrollment rates range from 95.6% to 97.4% [E2].
* **Grades 1–8 (Basic Education):** Total enrollment rates range from 109.3% to 120.4%, and net enrollment rates range from 87.6% to 96.1% [E2]. 
* **Gender Equality:** The Gender Equality Indicator in the net enrollment rate for Grades 1–8 ranges between 0.98 and 1.00 [E2].
* **Retention and Completion:** The retention rate in Grade 8 spans from 75.9% to 86.2%, and the completion rate of the basic education level ranges between 68.4% and 80.3% [E2].
* **Out-of-School Children:** The percentage of out-of-school children aged 5–12 years ranges from 10.6% down to 3.9% (with 4.9% also recorded) [E2].

### 2. Secondary and School Examinations
* **Secondary Education Examination (SEE / Regular SLC):** Historical pass rates prior to letter grading ranged between 38.72% (83,747 passed out of 216,303 appeared) and 68.47% (234,602 passed out of 342,632 appeared) [E5]. Under the letter grading system—introduced in the 2015 academic year for the technical line and 2016 for the general line—regular examination candidate counts ranged from 437,326 up to 495,648 (with 484,924 in the latest listed year) [E5].
* **Grade 11 and Grade 12 Examinations:** The survey details annual appeared and passed numbers for boys, girls, and total students [E3]. A letter grading system was introduced in Grade 11 starting in academic year 2017 and in Grade 12 starting in academic year 2018 [E1], [E3]. Grade 11 examinations were subsequently noted as being conducted from schools [E1], [E3].

### 3. School Scholarships
* All scholarship programs have been transferred to the local level, except those targeted at conflict victims, martyrs' children, and pro-poor targeted children [E5].
* Under details of scholarships for school children for FY 2022/23, figures recorded include 2,575,204; 2,388,188; 1,143,631; and 2,367,539 [E5].

### 4. Basic and Secondary Schools and Students Counts
* The survey includes an annex tracking the number of basic level (grades 1–5 and 6–8) and secondary level (grades 9–10 and 11–12) schools and students [E1]. However, because the text extraction for Annex 11.14 is malformed and unaligned, reliable mapping of individual school and student numerical counts to specific academic years and education levels cannot be determined from the passage [E1].

### 5. Higher Education / College Students
* For students attending colleges under various universities, total student enrollment increased over the reported years: 538,184 (2018/19); 546,279 (2019/20); 556,797 (2020/21); 682,589 (2021/22); and 739,941 (2022/23) [E4].

baseline_answer_text:
Under Article 35 (Right relating to Health), the Constitution of Nepal guarantees the following:

* **Free basic and emergency health services:** Every citizen has the right to free basic health services from the State, and no one shall be deprived of emergency health services [E2].
* **Information on medical treatment:** Every person has the right to get information about his or her medical treatment [E2].
* **Equal access:** Every citizen has equal access to health services [E2].
* **Clean drinking water and sanitation:** Every citizen has the right of access to clean drinking water and sanitation [E2].

Additionally, the Constitution provides other health-related guarantees:
* **Rights of women:** Every woman has the right to safe motherhood and reproductive health [E2], as well as the right to obtain special opportunities in health, education, employment, and social security on the basis of positive discrimination [E3].
* **Rights of children:** Every child has the right to health, education, maintenance, proper care, sports, entertainment, and overall personality development from their families and the State [E3].
* **Prioritized opportunities for specific groups:** Families of martyrs, disappeared persons, those who became disabled or injured in people's movements, armed conflicts, and revolutions, democracy fighters, conflict victims, displaced persons, persons with disabilities, and injured victims have the right to obtain prioritized opportunities in health, education, employment, housing, and social security, in accordance with law [E4].

* **Constitutional Right and Objective:** The Preamble notes that the Act makes necessary legal provisions to implement the right to get emergency health service (along with free basic health service) guaranteed by the Constitution of Nepal [E1].
* **Definition:** "Emergency health service" is defined as the initial and immediate service to be provided as necessary to free persons' lives from risk and save their lives or organs from being lost when their lives are in a risky condition upon falling into an unexpected incident or emergency condition [E1]. In addition, "service of general emergency condition" is listed as one of the headings of free basic health services that every citizen has the right to obtain as prescribed [E2].

If health insurance is not in effect or is insufficient to cover expenses, the costs are borne by the concerned person, their guardian, family member, patron, or the person accepting patronage [E3], [E5]. Based on the Public Health Service Act, 2075 (2018), the provisions regarding emergency health services are as follows:

### Definition and Scope
* **Definition:** "Emergency health service" is defined as the initial and immediate service to be provided as necessary to free persons from risk, and save lives or organs from being lost, whose lives are in a risky condition upon falling into an unexpected incident or emergency condition [E1].
* **Constitutional Right:** The Act's preamble references implementing the constitutional guarantee of the right to obtain free basic health service and emergency health service [E1]. Additionally, "service of general emergency condition" is categorized as one of the free basic health services that every citizen has the right to obtain [E2].

### Duties and Delivery of Emergency Treatment (Section 4)
* **Obligation to Provide:** Every health institution must provide emergency health service as prescribed [E2]. It is the explicit duty of each health institution and health worker to provide this service [E2].
* **Referral Requirement:** If emergency health service is not available at a health institution, that institution must first provide whatever treatment is available there and then refer the patient to another health institution for additional treatment [E3].
* **Treatment Before Administrative Process:** When providing emergency health service, the service recipient is required to complete the procedures/processes for obtaining such service only *after* treatment has commenced [E3], [E5].
* **Expenses:** 
  * Treatment expenses under Section 4 are borne by health insurance if available [E3], [E5].
  * If health insurance is not in effect or is insufficient to cover the expenses, the cost must be borne by the person concerned, their guardian, family member, patron, or the person who accepted patronage [E3], [E5].
  * However, the health institution must provide health services falling under basic health service free of charge [E3], [E5].
* Other provisions relating to emergency treatment services shall be as prescribed [E5].

### Emergency Health Service and Management (Section 48)
* **Teams and Groups:** A rapid response team and an emergency physicians' group shall exist as prescribed to extend health services immediately during emergency circumstances [E4].
* **Emergency Health Plans:** The Federal, Provincial, and Local Levels are required to develop and enforce emergency health plans [E4].
* **Standards:** These plans must be developed in consonance with standards and directives determined by the Government of Nepal under Federal law [E4].

baseline_answer_text:
Under the Public Health Service Act, 2075, the provisions regarding informed consent are as follows:

**Requirement and Definition**
* Every health institution must obtain the informed consent of the service recipient while providing him or her with health service [E2].
* "Informed consent" is defined as written or oral consent given by a person who is legally competent to obtain health service [E1], [E2].
* Written consent must be obtained to provide the prescribed treatment [E1], [E2].
* Providing treatment service without obtaining informed consent pursuant to Section 11 is prohibited [E3].

**Exceptions Where Service May Be Provided Without Informed Consent**
Health services may be provided without the informed consent of the service recipient in any of the following circumstances [E1]:
1. If the service recipient is not in a condition to give consent or has not authorized anyone else to give consent, and such consent is given by his or her wife or husband, father or mother, grandfather or grandmother, adult son or daughter, brother or sister (as far as available respectively), or the available closest person of the service recipient [E1].
2. If the health service is provided without consent under prevailing law or by a court order [E1].
3. If there is a serious threat likely to occur to public health if the person is not treated [E1].
4. If there is a possibility of death of the concerned patient or irreparable damage is likely to occur to his or her health if the provision of health service is delayed [E1].
5. If the concerned person has not refused to obtain health service in an expressed or unexpressed manner or by conduct [E1].
6. In other cases as prescribed [E1].

selected_evidence.chunk_text: साक्षरता ११.५९ चालु आर्थिकवर्षकोफागुनसम्ममामुगुरजुम्लाजिल्लाथपभईसाक्षरघोषणाभएका जिल्लाकोसङ्ख्या६६पुगेकोछ।हालसम्मकोशी, गण्डकीरबागमतीप्रदेशसाक्षर प्रदेशघोषणाभएकाछन्भनेसुदूरपश्चिमरलुम्बिनीप्रदेशसाक्षरप्रदेशकोरूपमाघोषणाको तयारीमारहेकाछन्। प्राविधिकतथाव्यावसायिकशिक्षा ११.६० चालुआर्थिकवर्ष २०८१/८२कोफागुनसम्मश्रमबजारकोआवश्यकतारमागबमोजिम ५,३६०जनाकोलागिनिःशुल्कछोटोअवधिकोसीपमूलकतालीमसञ्चालनभएका छन्। २०८१फागुनसम्मविभिन्नतहरपेशामासीपपरीक्षणप्रमाणीकृतभएका जनशक्तिकोसङ्ख्या४लाख९७हजार९सयभन्दाबढीरहेकोछ। विद्यालयदिवाखाजाकार्यक्रम ११.६१ दिवाखाजाकार्यक्रमबाटशैक्षिकसत्र२०८१मा प्रारम्भिकबालशिक्षादेखिकक्षा५ सम्मसामुदायिकविद्यालयमाअध्ययनरतदेशभरका२८लाख६हजार३सय१ विद्यार्थीप्रत्यक्षरूपमालाभान्वितभएकाछन्।गतशैक्षिकसत्रमा३०लाख९हजार ६सय४०विद्यार्थीप्रत्यक्षरूपमालाभान्वितभएकाथिए। ११.६२ बझाङ, बाजुरार दार्चुलाजिल्लाका१,०६६ सामुदायिकविद्यालयकाबालविकासदेखि कक्षा८सम्मकाबालबालिकाकालागिशिक्षाकालागिखाद्यकार्यक्रमबाटदिवाखाजाको व्यवस्थागरिएकोछ।

प्राक्कथन मुलुककोसमग्रआर्थिक, सामाजिकएवम्भौतिकविकासकोस्थितिसमेटिएकोआर्थिकसर्वेक्षण, २०८१/८२सार्वजनिकगरेकोFl यसमामुख्यरुपमाचालु आर्थिकवर्षकोप्रथमआठमहिना रगतआर्थिकवर्षकोमुलुककोसमग्रआर्थिकअवस्थाप्रस्तुतगरिएकोछ।संघ, प्रदेशरस्थानीय तहकोएकीकृतवित्तस्थितिकोविश्लेषणगरिएकोछ।सार्वभौमक्रेडिटरेटिङ्गस्कोरलेदेखाएको लगानीसम्भावनालगायतकाविषयसमेतसमावेशगरिएकोछ। मुलुककोआर्थिकवृद्धिदरचालुआर्थिकवर्ष४.६१प्रतिशतरहनेअनुमानछ। पेट्रोलियमपदार्थको मूल्यमाआएकोकमीरआपूर्तिश्रृङ्खलासहजरहेकालेऔसतउपभोक्तामुद्रास्फीति४.७२प्रतिशत रहेकोछ।राजस्वपरिचालनसुधारहुँदैगएकोले संघीयसरकारकोवित्तघाटाघटेकोछ।यस अवधिमासंघबाटप्रदेशरस्थानीयतहमाअनुदानरराजस्वबाँडफाँटसमेतगरीरु. ३खर्ब२५ अर्ब४६करोडहस्तान्तरणभएकोछ। वस्तु निकासीउच्चदरलेबढेकोछ।चालुखातारशोधनान्तरस्थितिदुवैबचतमाछन्।विदेशी बिनिमयसञ्चितिहालसम्मकै उच्चरहेकोछ। बाह्यक्षेत्रकासबैपरिसूचकसबलर सुदृढरही बाह्य क्षेत्रस्थिरताकायमभएकोछ।सबै स्थानीयतहमावाणिज्यबैंककोशाखापुगेकोछ। सूचनाप्रविधिकोविकाससँगै डिजिटलबैंकिङ्गकारोबारबढेकोछ।

baseline_answer_text:
आर्थिक सर्वेक्षणले विद्यालय र विद्यार्थी सङ्ख्याका सम्बन्धमा निम्न जानकारी दिएको छ:

**विद्यालय सम्बन्धी जानकारी:**
* **सामुदायिक विद्यालयको सङ्ख्या:** कुल विद्यालयमध्ये ७८.० प्रतिशत सामुदायिक विद्यालय रहेका छन् [E4]। विद्यालय नक्साङ्कन तथा समायोजनका कारण शैक्षिक सत्र २०८० को तुलनामा शैक्षिक सत्र २०८१ मा सामुदायिक विद्यालयको सङ्ख्यामा कमी आएको छ [E1]। सामुदायिक विद्यालयको कुल सङ्ख्या २७,२९८ रहेको छ [E1, E3]।
* **विद्यालयमा विद्यार्थीको वितरण:** कुल सामुदायिक विद्यालयमध्ये १०० भन्दा कम विद्यार्थी भएका विद्यालय ५५.९ प्रतिशत (१५,२७३ विद्यालय) र २ हजारभन्दा बढी विद्यार्थी भएका विद्यालय ०.४ प्रतिशत रहेका छन् [E1]। 
* सहरी क्षेत्रमा बढ्दै गएको बसाइँसराइ र जन्मदरमा आएको कमीले ग्रामीण क्षेत्रका विद्यालयमा विद्यार्थी सङ्ख्या कम हुँदै गएको देखिएको छ भने पछिल्लो समय केही सामुदायिक विद्यालयमा विद्यार्थी सङ्ख्या बढ्दै गएको पनि देखिएको छ [E1, E4]।

**विद्यार्थी सङ्ख्या सम्बन्धी जानकारी:**
* **सामुदायिक र संस्थागत विद्यालयमा विद्यार्थीको अनुपात:** शैक्षिक सत्र २०८१ मा ६६.२ प्रतिशत विद्यार्थी सामुदायिक विद्यालयमा र ३३.८ प्रतिशत विद्यार्थी संस्थागत विद्यालयमा अध्ययनरत छन् (शैक्षिक सत्र २०८० मा सामुदायिकमा ६९.९ प्रतिशत र संस्थागतमा ३०.१ प्रतिशत थिए) [E4]।
* **सामुदायिक विद्यालयको विद्यार्थी सङ्ख्या:** सामुदायिक विद्यालयमा अध्ययनरत कुल विद्यार्थी सङ्ख्या ४६,४२,७२९ रहेको छ [E3]। 
* **प्रति विद्यालय र प्रति शिक्षक अनुपात:** कक्षा १-१२ सम्मका विद्यार्थी सङ्ख्यालाई आधार मान्दा सामुदायिक विद्यालयमा प्रति विद्यालय विद्यार्थी सङ्ख्या १७० रहेको छ [E2]। त्यस्तै, सामुदायिक विद्यालयमा प्रति शिक्षक विद्यार्थी सङ्ख्या २४ रहेको छ [E2]।
* **तहगत विद्यार्थी हिस्सा:** कुल विद्यार्थीमध्ये आधारभूत तह (कक्षा १–५) मा ४९.४ प्रतिशत, आधारभूत तह (कक्षा ६–८) मा २५.८ प्रतिशत, माध्यमिक तह (कक्षा ९–१०) मा १३.९ प्रतिशत र माध्यमिक तह (कक्षा ११–१२) मा ९.५ प्रतिशत विद्यार्थी अध्ययनरत छन् [E5]।
* **लैङ्गिक विवरण:** शैक्षिक सत्र २०८१ मा (कक्षा १–१२ सम्म) कुल विद्यार्थीमध्ये छात्र ५१.९ प्रतिशत र छात्रा ४८.१ प्रतिशत रहेका छन् [E3, E5]। यस शैक्षिक सत्रमा कुल विद्यार्थी भर्नामा प्रति १०० छात्र बराबर भर्ना हुने छात्राको सङ्ख्या ९३ रहेको छ [E5]।

baseline_answer_text:
आर्थिक सर्वेक्षणमा बेरोजगारी तथा रोजगारी कार्यक्रमहरूका सम्बन्धमा देहायबमोजिमको जानकारी दिइएको छ:

**१. प्रधानमन्त्री रोजगार कार्यक्रम:**
* आर्थिक वर्ष २०८१/८२ को फागुनसम्म ७४३ स्थानीय तहमा ७ लाख ९७ हजार ७ सय २५ जना बेरोजगार व्यक्ति सूचीकृत भएका छन् [E1], [E3]। सूचीकृतमध्ये ४,२२३ जना रोजगारीमा संलग्न भएका छन् [E3]।
* यसअघि आर्थिक वर्ष २०८०/८१ मा ७३५ स्थानीय तहमा ८ लाख ८५ हजार १ सय ५३ बेरोजगार व्यक्ति सूचीकृत भएकोमा ६४ हजार ७ सय ३३ जनाले औसत ७९ दिनको रोजगारी प्राप्त गरेका थिए [E1], [E3]।
* चालु आर्थिक वर्षको फागुनसम्म औसत रोजगारी दिनको हिसाबले कर्णाली प्रदेशभित्रका स्थानीय तहले सबैभन्दा बढी र मधेश प्रदेशका स्थानीय तहले सबैभन्दा कम रोजगारी प्रदान गरेका छन् [E4]।

**२. उच्च पहाडी एवम् हिमाली क्षेत्र स्वरोजगार तथा आर्थिक-सामाजिक सशक्तीकरण कार्यक्रम:**
* मानव विकास सूचकाङ्कमा तुलनात्मक रूपमा पछाडि परेका उच्च पहाडी एवम् हिमाली क्षेत्रका स्थानीय तहलाई लक्षित गरी चालु आर्थिक वर्षदेखि यो कार्यक्रम सञ्चालनमा आएको छ [E1]।
* चालु आर्थिक वर्षमा यो कार्यक्रम सुदूरपश्चिम र कर्णाली प्रदेशका विभिन्न १३ जिल्लाका ६२ स्थानीय तहमा सञ्चालनमा रहेको छ [E1]।

**३. आन्तरिक रोजगारी दशक तथा श्रम सम्मेलन:**
* आर्थिक वर्ष २०८२/८३ देखि आर्थिक वर्ष २०९१/९२ सम्म "आन्तरिक रोजगारी दशक" घोषणा गरिएको छ [E1]।
* तीन तहका सरकार, निजी क्षेत्र, श्रमिक र विकास साझेदारको सहभागितामा २०८१ फागुनमा पाँचौं राष्ट्रिय श्रम तथा रोजगार सम्मेलन काठमाडौंमा सम्पन्न भएको छ [E1]।

**४. सुरक्षित आप्रवासन (सामी) कार्यक्रम:**
* संघ, प्रदेश र स्थानीय सरकारको साझेदारीमा सुरक्षित आप्रवासन (सामी) कार्यक्रम चौथो चरण (२०२४–२०२८) ६८ जिल्लाका २६७ स्थानीय तहमा सञ्चालनमा रहेको छ [E5]। यस कार्यक्रमबाट २०८१ फागुनसम्म ४ लाख ५४ हजार २ सय ३१ व्यक्तिले वैदेशिक रोजगार सम्बन्धी सेवा प्राप्त गरेका छन् [E5]।

baseline_answer_text:
Based on the Economic Survey, the reported literacy rates and related figures are as follows:

**Literacy Rates:**
* **Adult Literacy Rate:** In the assessment of criteria for graduation to a developing country, Nepal's adult literacy rate is reported at 71.15% against a threshold range of 25% to 100% [E1].
* **Age 15–24 Years:** The literacy rate for the 15–24 age group reached 94.2% (up from 88.6% in earlier years) [E4].
* **Age 15+ Years:** The literacy rate for ages 15 and above is reported at 71.2% (having previously stood at 58.0%) [E4].
* **General Literacy Rate (reported as 6- / 5+ years):** The literacy rate is listed at 76.3% for recent years (previously recorded at 78.x%) [E4].
* **Data Source Note:** The survey notes that literacy rates after 2079 were prepared on the basis of the census [E4].

**Literacy Declaration Status:**
* By Falgun of the current fiscal year, with the addition of Mugu and Jumla, the number of districts declared literate reached 66 [E3].
* Koshi, Gandaki, and Bagmati provinces have been declared literate provinces, while Sudurpashchim and Lumbini provinces are preparing for declaration as literate provinces [E3].
candidate_answer_text:
Based on the Economic Survey (आर्थिक सर्वेक्षण २०८१/८२), the reported literacy rates and related statistics for Nepal are as follows:

### Literacy Rates by Age Group
According to data sourced from the Ministry of Education, Science and Technology (based on the census after 2079) [E4]:
* **Ages 6 years and above (६+ वर्ष):** 76.3% for fiscal years 2079, 2080, and 2081 [E4].
* **Ages 15–24 years (१५–२४ वर्ष):** 94.2% for fiscal years 2079, 2080, and 2081 (up from 88.6% in 2077) [E4].
* **Ages 15 years and above (१५+ वर्ष):** 71.2% for fiscal years 2079, 2080, and 2081 [E4].

### Adult Literacy Rate (Graduation Criteria)
* Under the criteria for graduation to a developing country (sourced from the National Planning Commission, 2024), Nepal's adult literacy rate (प्रौढ साक्षरता दर) stands at **71.15%** (against a threshold range of 25 to 100) [E1].

### Literate District and Province Declarations
* By Falgun of the current fiscal year, with the addition of Mugu and Jumla districts, the total number of districts declared literate reached 66 [E3].
* Koshi, Gandaki, and Bagmati provinces have been declared literate provinces, while Sudurpashchim and Lumbini provinces are in preparation to be declared literate provinces [E3].

baseline_answer_text:
Based on the Economic Survey, the report details the following regarding schools and student numbers:

**School Distribution and Structure**
* **Community School Counts:** Total community schools stand at 27,298 [E1, E2]. School mapping and adjustment resulted in a reduction in the number of community schools in academic session 2081 compared to academic session 2080 [E1].
* **Share of Schools:** Community schools make up 78.0 percent of all schools [E5].
* **School Size by Student Enrollment:** Among community schools, 55.9 percent (15,273 schools) have fewer than 100 students, whereas only 0.4 percent have more than 2,000 students [E1]. 
* **Enrollment Trends:** Decreases in rural school student numbers are attributed to increasing urban migration and declining birth rates [E1]. However, student numbers have recently been seen rising in certain community schools [E5].
* **Specialized Schools:** To expand educational access for children with disabilities, 33 special schools, 23 integrated schools, and 380 resource classes were operational by Falgun 2081 [E4].

**Student Enrollment and Demographics**
* **Community vs. Institutional Enrollment:** Total student enrollment across community schools is 4,642,729 [E2]. In academic session 2081, 66.2 percent of students were enrolled in community schools and 33.6 percent in institutional schools, compared to 69.9 percent in community schools and 30.1 percent in institutional schools in academic session 2080 [E5].
* **Level-wise Student Distribution:** Out of total students, 49.4 percent are at the basic level (grades 1–5), 25.8 percent at the basic level (grades 6–8), 13.9 percent at the secondary level (grades 9–10), and 9.5 percent at the secondary level (grades 11–12) [E3].
* **Gender Ratio:** In academic session 2081, female students accounted for 48.1 percent and male students accounted for 51.9 percent of total enrollment [E3]. For every 100 boys enrolled in grades 1–12, there were 93 girls enrolled [E3].

**Higher Education Students**
* In academic session 2080, student numbers in higher education grew by 9.86 percent to reach 672,489 (up from 601,783 in academic session 2079) [E4].
* Among higher education students, 74.31 percent study at Tribhuvan University (26.39 percent in constituent campuses and 47.92 percent in affiliated campuses), while 25.69 percent are enrolled in other universities, health science academies, or foreign-affiliated campuses [E4].
baseline_review_notes: unlike Q14, it correctly says 33.6%, but it misses the primary gold passage's important ratios such as approximately 170 students per community school and 24 students per teacher.
candidate_answer_text:
Based on the Economic Survey (*आर्थिक सर्वेक्षण २०८१/८२*), the reported details regarding schools and student numbers are as follows:

### School Numbers and Trends
* **Community school reduction:** The number of community schools decreased in the academic session 2081 compared to 2080 due to school mapping and adjustment/merging [E1]. 
* **Total community schools:** There are a total of 27,298 community schools [E1, E2].
* **Share of schools:** Community schools account for 78.0% of total schools [E5].
* **Special and integrated schools:** For children with disabilities, 33 special schools, 23 integrated schools, and 380 resource classes were operating by Falgun 2081 [E4].
*(Note: Some specific sub-level counts in Table 11(ट) are malformed/garbled in the text) [E1].*

### Distribution of Community Schools by Student Enrollment
* **Small schools:** 55.9% of all community schools have fewer than 100 students (totaling 15,273 schools) [E1].
* **Large schools:** Only 0.4% of community schools have more than 2,000 students [E1].
* **Rural decline:** Increasing migration to urban areas and a declining birth rate have led to declining student numbers in rural community schools [E1].

### Student Numbers and Share by School Type
* **Community school students:** In community schools, there are a total of 4,642,729 students [E2]. By level, community schools enroll:
  * Basic level (Grades 1–5): 2,187,449 students [E2]
  * Basic level (Grades 1–8): 1,274,154 students *(table text contains garbled character: १२७४१%५४)* [E2]
  * Secondary level (Grades 1–10): 729,569 students [E2]
  * Secondary level (Grades 1–12): 451,557 students [E2]
* **Community vs. institutional distribution:** In academic session 2081, 66.2% of students study in community schools and 33.8% in institutional schools, compared to 69.9% in community and 30.1% in institutional schools in academic session 2080 [E5].

### Level-Wise Distribution of Total Students
Across community and institutional schools, a decline in student numbers has been estimated due to a decrease in the school-age population [E3]. 
* **Level breakdown:** Of the total students, 49.4% are in Basic level (Grades 1–5), 25.8% in Basic level (Grades 6–8), 13.9% in Secondary level (Grades 9–10), and 9.5% in Secondary level (Grades 11–12) [E3].
* **5-year trend (Academic session 2081 numbers):**
  * Basic level (Grades 1–5): 3,514,928 [E3]
  * Basic level (Grades 6–8): 1,832,140 [E3]
  * Secondary level (Grades 9–10): 989,885 [E3]
  * Secondary level (Grades 11–12): 673,855 [E3]
  * Total enrollment across grades 1–12: 7,010,808 [E3]

### Gender Breakdown
* In academic session 2081 (Grades 1–12), 48.1% of enrolled students are female and 51.9% are male [E2, E3] *(note: passage [E2] also contains a typographical rendering of male students as 91.9%)*.
* For every 100 male students enrolled in grades 1–12, 93 female students are enrolled [E3].

### Higher Education Student Numbers
* In academic session 2079, there were 601,783 students in higher education [E4].
* In academic session 2080, higher education enrollment increased by 9.86% to 672,489 students [E4].

### Agricultural and Non-Agricultural Growth
* **Current Fiscal Year (FY 2081/82):** Agricultural sector production (gross value added) is estimated to grow by 3.28% [E1], [E4], while non-agricultural sector production is estimated to grow by 4.28% [E1] (also cited as 4.2% in [E4]). Paddy production is estimated to increase by 4.04% [E1], [E4].
* **Previous Fiscal Year:** Agricultural sector production grew by 3.35%, and non-agricultural sector production grew by 3.36% [E1], [E4].

---

### Sector Contributions to GDP

#### 1. Agricultural vs. Non-Agricultural Sector
* Since FY 2079/80, the contribution of the non-agricultural sector to GDP has declined, while the contribution of the agricultural sector has increased [E2].
* **Current Fiscal Year:** The agricultural sector is estimated to contribute 25.2% and the non-agricultural sector 74.8% [E2].
* **Previous Fiscal Year:** The contributions were 24.7% for agriculture and 75.3% for non-agriculture [E2].
* **Last Decade Average:** The average contribution was 25.5% for agriculture and 74.5% for non-agriculture [E2].

#### 2. Agriculture, Industry, and Service Sectors
* The service sector maintains the highest contribution to GDP [E1].
* **Current Fiscal Year:** 
  * Agriculture sector: Estimated at 25.16% [E1], [E3], [E5].

  * Service sector: Estimated at 62.01% [E1], [E5].
* **Previous Fiscal Year:** 
  * Agriculture sector: 24.71% [E1], [E3], [E5].
  * Industry sector: 12.91% [E1], [E5] (with mining and quarrying at 0.48% [E3]).
  * Service sector: 62.38% [E1], [E5].

#### 3. Primary, Secondary, and Service Sectors Classification
* In the current fiscal year, the contributions of the secondary and service sectors decreased, whereas the contribution of the primary sector increased [E5].
* **Current Fiscal Year:** Primary sector contribution is estimated at 25.62%, secondary sector at 12.37%, and service sector at 62.01% [E5].
* **Previous Fiscal Year:** Primary sector contribution was 25.19%, secondary sector was 12.43%, and service sector was 62.38% [E5].
* **Last Decade Average:** The annual average contributions stood at 26.07% for the primary sector, 13.42% for the secondary sector, and 60.51% for the service sector [E5].

candidate_answer_text:
Based on the Economic Survey (2081/82), the reports concerning health services and health institutions in Nepal include the following:

### Health Institutions
* **Total Government Health Institutions:** By Falgun, the total number of government health institutions reached 8,746 [E1]. This includes:
  * Hospitals: 345 [E1]
  * Primary Health Centres: 149 [E1]
  * Health Posts: 3,742 [E1]
  * Other health institutions: 4,510 [E1]

### Health Human Resources
* As of Falgun 2081, Nepal has 1.1 doctors and 2.86 nurses per 1,000 population [E1], [E4].

### Health Services, Insurance, and Targeted Care
* **Free Treatment for Destitute Citizens:** By Falgun of the current fiscal year, 37,984 impoverished/destitute citizens received health services, including free medicines, for the treatment of heart, cancer, and kidney diseases [E1].
* **Health Insurance:** 49.2 percent of the insured population has utilized health insurance services [E1].
* **Maternal and Child Health Services:**
  * The proportion of pregnant women receiving regular antenatal checkups and having deliveries attended by skilled birth attendants has increased [E2]. Deliveries assisted by skilled birth attendants stood at 36.0% (Census 2068) and 58.0% (UN projection-based) [E4].
  * Deliveries taking place in health institutions reached 77.9 percent according to the Health Management Information System (HMIS), compared to 35.3 percent based on Census 2068 and 57.4 percent based on UN projections [E4].
  * The proportion of children who are fully vaccinated has increased [E2]. Under basic antigens, coverage is recorded at 87.0% (Census 2068) and 77.8% (UN projection) [E4].

### Health Outcomes and Strategic Assessment
* **Life Expectancy:** The average life expectancy of citizens has reached 71.3 years [E2], [E4].
* **Fertility Rate:** The total fertility rate is reported at 1.95 per woman based on the Health Management Information System [E4] (and 2.1 per woman in 2024 according to SDG target tracking) [E5].
* **Service Delivery Status:** Nepal's achievements under the "healthy life" objective are reported as satisfactory, but additional efforts are needed to control communicable diseases such as tuberculosis and malaria and to ensure that essential health services are easily accessible [E5].

baseline_answer_text:
Based on the provided documents from the Economic Survey, the following details are reported regarding unemployment and employment programmes:

**Prime Minister Employment Programme (PMEP) and Unemployment Registration:**
* By Falgun of the fiscal year 2081/82, a total of 797,725 unemployed individuals were registered across 743 local levels under the Prime Minister Employment Programme [E1]. 
* In the previous fiscal year (2080/81), 885,153 unemployed individuals were registered across 735 local levels, of whom 64,733 individuals received employment for an average of 79 days [E1].
* Based on the average days of employment generated through the Prime Minister Employment Programme up to Falgun of the current fiscal year, local levels in Karnali Province provided the highest average days of employment, whereas local levels in Madhesh Province provided the lowest [E5].

**High Mountain and Hilly Region Self-Employment Programme:**
* Starting in the current fiscal year, the "High Mountain and Hilly Region Self-Employment and Socio-Economic Empowerment Programme" was launched, targeting local levels in high hilly and mountainous areas that comparatively lag behind in the Human Development Index [E1]. 
* In the current fiscal year, this programme is being implemented in 62 local levels across 13 districts of Sudurpashchim and Karnali Provinces [E1].

**National Conferences and Strategic Declarations:**
* In Falgun 2081, the Fifth National Labour and Employment Conference was held in Kathmandu with the participation of three tiers of government, the private sector, workers, and development partners [E1].
* The period from fiscal year 2082/83 to fiscal year 2091/92 has been declared the "Internal Employment Decade" [E1].

**Foreign Employment, Social Security, and Overall Impact:**
* The number of Nepali workers obtaining labor approvals for foreign employment has surpassed 6.4 million [E2].
* Approximately 2.08 million workers from the formal sector, foreign employment, informal sector, and self-employment sectors have been registered in the Social Security Fund [E2].
* Employment- and poverty-alleviation-targeted programmes, along with education and skill-enhancement initiatives for underprivileged groups, contributed to lowering the poverty rate (population living on less than $1.90 US per day) to 20.27% and multidimensional poverty to 17.4% in 2024 [E3].
candidate_answer_text:
Based on the Economic Survey (2081/82), the following details are reported regarding unemployment and employment programmes:

### Prime Minister Employment Programme (PMEP) and Unemployment
* **FY 2081/82:** Up to Falgun of FY 2081/82, a total of 797,725 unemployed individuals were registered across 743 local levels under the Prime Minister Employment Programme [E1].
* **FY 2080/81:** In FY 2080/81, 885,153 unemployed individuals were registered across 735 local levels, and 64,733 individuals received employment for an average of 79 days [E1].
* **Provincial Comparison:** Up to Falgun of the current fiscal year, measured by average employment days, local levels in Karnali Province provided the highest employment, while local levels in Madhesh Province provided the least employment under the programme [E5].

### High Hill and Mountain Area Self-Employment and Socio-Economic Empowerment Programme
* Launched in the current fiscal year, this programme targets local levels in high hill and mountainous regions that lag comparatively in the Human Development Index [E1].
* In the current fiscal year, it is being implemented across 62 local levels in 13 districts of Sudurpashchim Province and Karnali Province [E1].

### Policy Initiatives and Labour Highlights
* **Internal Employment Decade:** The period from FY 2082/83 to FY 2091/92 has been declared the "Internal Employment Decade" [E1].
* **National Labour and Employment Conference:** The Fifth National Labour and Employment Conference was held in Kathmandu in Falgun 2081 with participation from the three tiers of government, the private sector, workers, and development partners [E1].
* **Foreign Employment and Social Security:** The number of Nepali workers taking labour approvals for foreign employment has exceeded 6.4 million [E2]. Additionally, approximately 2,080,000 workers across the formal, informal, foreign employment, and self-employment sectors have been enrolled in the Social Security Fund [E2].

gold_reference_evidence.chunk_text: ६.६ मानवविकाससूचकाङ्कमातुलनात्मकरूपमापछाडिपरेकाउच्चपहाडीएवम्हिमाली क्षेत्रकास्थानीयतहलाईलक्षितगरीचालु आर्थिकवर्षदेखि"उच्चपहाडीएवम्हिमाली क्षेत्रस्वरोजगारतथाआर्थिक-सामाजिकसशक्तीकरणकार्यक्रम" सञ्चालनमाआएकोछ। चालु आर्थिकवर्षसुदूरपश्चिमरकर्णालीप्रदेशकाविभिन्न१३जिल्लाका६२स्थानीय तहमायसकार्यक्रमसञ्चालनमारहेकोछ। ६.७ "प्रधानमन्त्रीरोजगारकार्यक्रम" अन्तर्गतआर्थिकवर्ष२०८१/८२कोफागुनसम्म ७४३स्थानीयतहमा ७लाख९७हजार७सय२५जनाबेरोजगारव्यक्तिसूचीकृत भएकाछन्। आर्थिकवर्ष२०८०/८१मा७३५स्थानीयतहमा ८लाख८५हजार १सय५३बेरोजगारव्यक्तिसूचीकृतभएकोमा६४हजार७सय३३जनालेऔसत ७९दिनकोरोजगारीप्राप्तगरेकाथिए। श्रम ६.८ तीनतहकासरकार, निजी क्षेत्र, श्रमिकरविकाससाझेदारसमेतकोसहभागितामा २०८१फागुनमापाँचौराष्ट्रियश्रमतथारोजगारसम्मेलनकाठमाडौंमासम्पन्नभएको छ। आर्थिकवर्ष२०८२/८३देखिआर्थिकवर्ष२०९१/९२सम्मआन्तरिकरोजगारी दशकघोषणाभएकोछ।

नेपालको संविधानको धारा ३५ (स्वास्थ्यसम्बन्धी हक) अन्तर्गत देहाय बमोजिमका व्यवस्थाहरू गरिएका छन्:

१. प्रत्येक नागरिकलाई राज्यबाट आधारभूत स्वास्थ्य सेवा निःशुल्क प्राप्त गर्ने हक हुनेछ र कसैलाई पनि आकस्मिक स्वास्थ्य सेवाबाट वञ्चित गरिने छैन [E1]।  
२. प्रत्येक व्यक्तिलाई आफ्नो स्वास्थ्य उपचारको सम्बन्धमा जानकारी पाउने हक हुनेछ [E1]।  
३. प्रत्येक नागरिकलाई स्वास्थ्य सेवामा समान पहुँचको हक हुनेछ [E1]।  
४. प्रत्येक नागरिकलाई स्वच्छ खानेपानी तथा सरसफाइमा पहुँचको हक हुनेछ [E1]।  

यसका अतिरिक्त संविधानमा स्वास्थ्यसँग सम्बन्धित देहायका अधिकारहरू समेत समावेश छन्:
- प्रत्येक महिलालाई सुरक्षित मातृत्व र प्रजनन स्वास्थ्यसम्बन्धी हक हुनेछ [E1]।  
- विपन्न नागरिक तथा लोपोन्मुख समुदायका नागरिकलाई उनीहरूको संरक्षण, उत्थान, सशक्तीकरण र विकासका लागि स्वास्थ्य लगायतका क्षेत्रमा विशेष अवसर तथा लाभ पाउने हक हुनेछ [E3]।

Chapter-1 Preliminary 1. Short title and commencement: (1) This Act may be cited as the "Public Health Service Act, 2075 (2018)."

(b) "Basic health service" means promotional, retributive, diagnostic, remedial and rehabilitative service easily and freely available from the state for the sake of fulfillment of health need of citizens generally, pursuant to sub-section (4) of Section 3. baseline_answer_text:
जनस्वास्थ्य सेवा ऐन, २०७५ ले आकस्मिक स्वास्थ्य सेवा सम्बन्धमा देहायबमोजिमका व्यवस्थाहरू गरेको छ:

**१. परिभाषा तथा संवैधानिक हकको कार्यान्वयन:**
* नेपालको संविधानद्वारा प्रत्याभूत निःशुल्क आधारभूत स्वास्थ्य सेवा र आकस्मिक स्वास्थ्य सेवा प्राप्त गर्ने हकलाई कार्यान्वयन गर्न यो ऐन जारी गरिएको हो [E1]।
* अप्रत्याशित घटना वा आपत्कालीन अवस्थामा परी ज्यान जोखिमपूर्ण अवस्थामा रहेका व्यक्तिको ज्यान जोखिममुक्त गर्न, ज्यान वा अङ्ग गुम्नबाट बचाउन आवश्यक प्रारम्भिक तथा तत्काल प्रदान गरिने सेवालाई "आकस्मिक स्वास्थ्य सेवा" भनिएको छ [E1]।

**२. आकस्मिक उपचारको व्यवस्था र कर्तव्य:**
* प्रत्येक स्वास्थ्य संस्थाले तोकिएबमोजिम आकस्मिक स्वास्थ्य सेवा उपलब्ध गराउनुपर्नेछ [E3]। 
* यस्तो सेवा उपलब्ध गराउनु प्रत्येक स्वास्थ्य संस्था र स्वास्थ्यकर्मीको कर्तव्य हुनेछ [E3]।
* आकस्मिक स्वास्थ्य सेवा प्रदान गर्दा सम्बन्धित सेवाग्राहीले त्यस्तो सेवा प्राप्त गर्न पूरा गर्नुपर्ने प्रक्रिया उपचार प्रारम्भ गरेपछि मात्र पूरा गराउनुपर्ने व्यवस्था छ [E2]।

**३. उपचार खर्च र निःशुल्क सेवा:**
* आकस्मिक उपचारको खर्च स्वास्थ्य बीमा गरिएको भए सोहीबाट र स्वास्थ्य बीमा नभएको वा बीमा रकम अपुग भएको अवस्थामा सम्बन्धित व्यक्ति, निजको अभिभावक, परिवारको सदस्य, संरक्षक वा संरक्षण स्वीकार गरेको व्यक्तिले व्यहोर्नुपर्नेछ [E2]।
* यद्यपि, आधारभूत स्वास्थ्य सेवाअन्तर्गत पर्ने स्वास्थ्य सेवा भने स्वास्थ्य संस्थाले निःशुल्क उपलब्ध गराउनुपर्नेछ [E2]। प्रत्येक नागरिकलाई सामान्य आकस्मिक अवस्थाको सेवासहितका आधारभूत स्वास्थ्य सेवा निःशुल्क पाउने हक छ [E3]।
* आकस्मिक उपचार सेवासम्बन्धी अन्य व्यवस्थाहरू तोकिएबमोजिम हुने उल्लेख छ [E2]।

**४. आकस्मिक स्वास्थ्य सेवा तथा व्यवस्थापन:**
* आपत्कालीन परिस्थितिमा तत्काल स्वास्थ्य सेवा विस्तार गर्न तोकिएबमोजिम एक द्रुत प्रतिकार्य टोली (rapid response team) र आकस्मिक चिकित्सक समूह (emergency physicians' group) रहने व्यवस्था छ [E4]।
* संघ, प्रदेश र स्थानीय तहले आकस्मिक स्वास्थ्य योजना तर्जुमा गरी लागू गर्नुपर्नेछ [E4]। यस्तो योजना बनाउँदा संघीय कानूनबमोजिम नेपाल सरकारले निर्धारण गरेको मापदण्ड तथा निर्देशिका अनुकूल हुने गरी बनाउनुपर्नेछ [E4]।

**५. दुर्घटना वा अन्य कारणले बिरामी ल्याइएको अवस्था:**
* दुर्घटना वा अन्य कुनै कारणले उपचारका लागि कुनै स्वास्थ्य संस्थामा ल्याइएको व्यक्तिलाई स्वास्थ्य संस्थामा तत्काल उपलब्ध उपचार सेवा प्रदान गर्नुपर्नेछ र पहिचान नखुलेमा सोको सूचना सम्बन्धित स्थानीय प्रशासनलाई दिनुपर्नेछ [E5]।

The Public Health Service Act, 2075 (2018) Date of Authentication 2075/6/2 (18 September 2018) Act Number 11 of the year 2075 (2018) An Act Made to Provide for Public Health Service Preamble: Whereas, it is expedient to make necessary legal provisions for implementing the right to get free basic health service and emergency health service guaranteed by the Constitution of Nepal and establishing access of the citizens to health service by making it regular, effective, qualitative and easily available, Now, therefore, be it enacted by the Federal Parliament.

Chapter-1 Preliminary 1. Short title and commencement: (1) This Act may be cited as the "Public Health Service Act, 2075 (2018)."

(2) This Act shall come into force immediately. 2. Definitions: Unless the subject or the context otherwise requires, in this Act- (a) "Emergency health service" means the initial and immediate service to be provided as it is necessary to free the lives of the persons from risk, save the lives or organs from being lost, whose lives are in the risky condition upon falling into unexpected incident or emergency condition. (b) "Basic health service" means promotional, retributive, diagnostic, remedial and rehabilitative service easily and freely available from the state for the sake of fulfillment of health need of citizens generally, pursuant to sub-section (4) of Section 3. (c) "Non-governmental or private health institution" means a health institution operated with the investment and ownership of the non-governmental or private sector, upon receiving permission under the prevailing law. (d) "Physician" means a person registered in the concerned Council as a physician under the prevailing law. (e) "Public health supervisor" means the office-bearer designated for monitoring and regulation related to public health.

Provided that the health institution shall provide the health service under the basic health service without charge.

baseline_answer_text:
जनस्वास्थ्य सेवा ऐनअनुसार उपचारका लागि सूचित सहमति (informed consent) सम्बन्धी देहायबमोजिमका व्यवस्थाहरू छन्:

* **सूचित सहमति लिनुपर्ने:** प्रत्येक स्वास्थ्य संस्थाले सेवाग्राहीलाई स्वास्थ्य सेवा प्रदान गर्दा निजको सूचित सहमति लिनुपर्ने व्यवस्था छ [E2]। साथै, तोकिएको उपचार प्रदान गर्नका लागि लिखित सहमति लिनुपर्नेछ [E1], [E2]।
* **सूचित सहमतिको अर्थ:** स्वास्थ्य सेवा प्राप्त गर्न कानुनी रूपमा सक्षम व्यक्तिले दिएको लिखित वा मौखिक सहमतिलाई "सूचित सहमति" भनिएको छ [E1], [E2]।
* **सूचित सहमतिबिना स्वास्थ्य सेवा दिन सकिने अवस्थाहरू:** देहायका कुनै पनि परिस्थितिमा सेवाग्राहीको सूचित सहमतिबिना पनि स्वास्थ्य सेवा प्रदान गर्न सकिनेछ [E1]:
  * सेवाग्राही सहमति दिन सक्ने अवस्थामा नरहेमा वा त्यस्तो सहमति दिने अनुमति वा अधिकार कसैलाई नदिएको अवस्थामा, उपलब्ध भएसम्म क्रमशः निजको पति वा पत्नी, बाबु वा आमा, बाजे वा बज्यै, उमेर पुगेको छोरा वा छोरी, दाजुभाइ वा दिदीबहिनी वा उपलब्ध भएसम्म सेवाग्राहीको नजिकको व्यक्तिले सहमति दिएमा [E1],
  * प्रचलित कानुनबमोजिम वा अदालतको आदेशद्वारा सहमतिबिना नै स्वास्थ्य सेवा प्रदान गरिएको भएमा [E1],
  * कुनै व्यक्तिको उपचार नगरिएमा जनस्वास्थ्यमा गम्भीर खतरा उत्पन्न हुन सक्ने सम्भावना भएमा [E1],
  * स्वास्थ्य सेवा दिन ढिलाइ भएमा सम्बन्धित बिरामीको मृत्यु हुन सक्ने वा निजको स्वास्थ्यमा अपूरणीय क्षति पुग्न सक्ने सम्भावना भएमा [E1],
  * सम्बन्धित व्यक्तिले प्रत्यक्ष वा अप्रत्यक्ष रूपमा वा आफ्नो आचरणद्वारा स्वास्थ्य सेवा लिन इन्कार नगरेको अवस्था भएमा [E1],
  * तोकिएबमोजिमका अन्य अवस्थामा [E1]।
* **कसुर सम्बन्धी व्यवस्था:** दफा ११ बमोजिम सूचित सहमति नलिई उपचार सेवा प्रदान गर्नु यस ऐनअन्तर्गत कसुर/निषेधित कार्य मानिन्छ [E4]।
candidate_answer_text:
जनस्वास्थ्य सेवा ऐन, २०७५ अनुसार उपचारका लागि सूचित सहमति (Informed Consent) सम्बन्धी देहायबमोजिमका व्यवस्थाहरू रहेका छन्:

* **सूचित सहमति लिनुपर्ने:** प्रत्येक स्वास्थ्य संस्थाले सेवाग्राहीलाई स्वास्थ्य सेवा उपलब्ध गराउँदा निजको सूचित सहमति लिनुपर्नेछ [E2]।
* **सूचित सहमतिको परिभाषा:** स्वास्थ्य सेवा प्राप्त गर्न कानुनी रूपमा सक्षम व्यक्तिले दिएको लिखित वा मौखिक सहमतिलाई "सूचित सहमति" भनिएको छ [E1], [E2]।
* **लिखित सहमति आवश्यक हुने:** तोकिएको उपचार सेवा उपलब्ध गराउनका लागि लिखित सहमति नै लिनुपर्नेछ [E1], [E2]।
* **सूचित सहमति नलिई उपचार सेवा दिनु कसुर हुने:** ऐनको दफा ११ बमोजिम सूचित सहमति नलिई उपचार सेवा उपलब्ध गराउनु गैरकानुनी/निषेधित कार्य मानिन्छ [E4]।

**सूचित सहमति बिना नै स्वास्थ्य सेवा दिन सकिने अपवादात्मक अवस्थाहरू:**  
कुनै पनि सेवाग्राहीको सूचित सहमति बिना पनि देहायका अवस्थाहरूमा स्वास्थ्य सेवा प्रदान गर्न सकिनेछ [E1]:
1. सेवाग्राही स्वयं सहमति दिन सक्ने अवस्थामा नभएमा वा कसैलाई सहमति दिने अधिकार नदिएको भएमा, क्रमशः निजको उपलब्ध भएसम्म पति वा पत्नी, बाबु वा आमा, बाजे वा बज्यै, बालिग छोरा वा छोरी, दाजु वा भाइ, दिदी वा बहिनी वा उपलब्ध भएसम्मका निजको नजिकको व्यक्तिले सहमति दिएमा [E1]।
2. प्रचलित कानुनबमोजिम वा अदालतको आदेशद्वारा सहमति बिना स्वास्थ्य सेवा प्रदान गरिएको अवस्थामा [E1]।
3. कुनै व्यक्तिको उपचार नगरिएमा जनस्वास्थ्यमा गम्भीर खतरा उत्पन्न हुन सक्ने अवस्था भएमा [E1]।
4. स्वास्थ्य सेवा उपलब्ध गराउन ढिलाइ भएमा सम्बन्धित बिरामीको मृत्यु हुन सक्ने वा निजको स्वास्थ्यमा अपूरणीय क्षति पुग्न सक्ने सम्भावना भएमा [E1]।
5. सम्बन्धित व्यक्तिले व्यक्त वा अव्यक्त रूपमा अथवा आफ्नो आचरणद्वारा स्वास्थ्य सेवा लिन अस्वीकार नगरेको भएमा [E1]।
6. तोकिएका अन्य अवस्थाहरूमा [E1]।
